picks.editorial_note: An ARPA-H award of up to $53 million is one of the largest funding commitments in this batch, and pairs generative AI compound discovery with a concrete agricultural/safety goal — a strong signal of federal investment in AI-driven chemistry.
picks.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers

picks.editorial_note: WorldParticle, from MIT and UBC, is a single model that simulates wildly different physical phenomena (granular flow to protein folding) within one framework — a genuine step toward general-purpose physical simulation via AI.
picks.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins

picks.editorial_note: CSIRO's machine-learning imaging technique independently confirmed the landmark Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87 black hole and was published in Nature, lending AI-based methods new credibility in fundamental astrophysics.
picks.title: New CSIRO technique confirms iconic black hole image

picks.editorial_note: MIT CSAIL and CMU's 'Workspace Models' give robots a new memory mechanism to recall past observations cheaply, addressing a core bottleneck in robot learning for complex, multi-step skills.
picks.title: A new form of memory helps robots learn complex skills

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's MoU with robotics maker Unitree, anchored to a planned joint laboratory, is a notable academia-industry tie-up in embodied AI that could shape talent pipelines and product development in the field.
picks.title: HKUST and Unitree Sign MoU to Advance Embodied AI and Robotics Collaboration
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: Atos and Inria's strategic partnership to commercialize sovereign AI research (physical AI, agentic AI, cybersecurity) reflects a broader European push to convert academic AI research into national industrial capability.
picks.title: Atos and Inria enter into a strategic partnership to accelerate the transfer of research into sovereign industrial applications

picks.editorial_note: SMU's $4.2 million NIST-backed Digital Twin Technology Lab links AI, robotics, and HPC directly to semiconductor manufacturing workforce needs, a priority area for U.S. industrial policy.
picks.title: SMU awarded $4.2 million to advance AI-driven manufacturing and workforce training

picks.editorial_note: Allegations tying Nvidia's CEO to a suspected espionage case raise national-security questions about the AI hardware supply chain at a moment when chip access is central to AI policy debates.
picks.title: Nvidia CEO’s scandal raises questions about US national security

picks.editorial_note: A proposed $1 billion, 15-year AI investment for frontline social-service workers prompted experts to weigh real risks to vulnerable populations — a concrete case of AI policy intersecting with social welfare systems.
picks.title: Experts Explore How AI Could Affect Vulnerable Communities, Social Service Providers - UConn Today

picks.editorial_note: TU Wien's analysis of a 15-year-old recidivism-risk algorithm used in Catalonia shows that equally 'accurate' models can produce very different risk judgments, a finding with direct implications for AI use in criminal justice policy.
picks.title: In case of doubt, opt for the lower risk
